messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Increased 5xx and tail latency from inference pool in az1a. Autoscale muted. Suspected network interface churn. Paging on-call.
maria: I'm oncall, looking at metrics and ENI events. pulling logs.
leo: I see a burst of ENI detach/attach around the same time, some instances failing health checks.
maria: stack traces show repeated ip rewrite errors, packets looping to same host. possible multipath + stale routing cache.
ben: customer-impact: preliminary - ~8% errors for hosted API in eu-west routed to az1a. A few customers report elevated latency.
maria: running quick query: `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=availability-zone,Values=az1a Name=status,Values=in-use` to correlate.
leo: confirmed a set of ENIs showing detach events without instance termination. looks like ghost attachments.
ashley: @maria @leo do we have cross-az fallback enabled? we should start steering traffic to eu2 if safe.
maria: starting routing fallback to eu2 for inference routes for tier=hosted-low by flipping router policy (safe, no schema change).
networking-team: observed NAT rewrite mismatch causing some sessions to appear from unexpected IP — NLB health checks flapping.
ben: notifying support: top 3 affected customers (ids redacted) with brief note + mitigation steps. cust-success: preparing customer communication.
cust-success: draft sent to legal for review. will send within 10m.
maria: mitigation step 1: purge local route cache on affected nodes: `sudo systemctl restart redwood-routing` rolling 10% at a time.
leo: mitigation step 2: temporarily disable source-based ip rewrite on the nat-proxy fleet in az1a to prevent loops.
maria: applied iptables rule to drop the looped flows on the first batch. error rate down ~40% on those nodes.
incident-bot: automatic reroute policy triggered: route-group inference-hosted shifted 35% traffic to eu2 and usw2.
ben: tracking: customers impacted moved from 8% -> 3% of global requests after reroute.
networking-team: diving deeper — ENI attach failures due to controlplane API timeouts. cross-checking cloud provider status.
sre-lead: escalate to platform networking engineers if ENI churn continues after restart.
maria: starting a targeted drain of 6 affected nodes and forcing a fresh ENI attach lifecycle.
leo: warming KV cache on fallback nodes to reduce cold-start latency.
ashley: preparing oncall handoff in 25m. any outstanding tasks to pass?
maria: will continue automated restarts until churn stops. if stable for 15m, handoff is ok.
ben: customer impact note: support message queued, will include that routing fallback is active and we are monitoring.
cust-success: sent notifications to the top 3; they acknowledged.
networking-team: cloud provider status shows transient control-plane errors in az1a for ENI operations. filing ticket with provider.
sre-lead: add postmortem placeholder and link to incident runbook.
maria: status update: error rate down to ~1.2%, latency p95 returning to normal on most routes. still seeing sporadic ENI detach events but no immediate customer impact.
leo: confirm that no data plane consistency issues seen; no evidence of secret/key leakage.
maria: preparing final state change: re-enable rewrite on nat-proxy after route purge, monitored for 10m.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: AUTO: reroute rollback scheduled if metrics remain stable for 10m.
ashley: noted for handoff. I'll take on-call in 25m from now. handoff will include runbook steps for route purge and ENI lifecycle.
maria: handoff summary (to pass): cause = controlplane ENI attach timeout -> ghost attachments -> ip rewrite mismatch -> routing loops -> 5xx spike. mitigations applied: route fallback, targeted node restarts, iptables loop drop, nat-proxy rewrite disabled, KV warm-up on fallback nodes. customers notified.
sre-lead: thanks team. open action: provider ticket + postmortem + add ENI healthcheck stricter thresholds to avoid half-attached state.
maria: leaving thread to ashley for next 2h watch. tagging `#postmortems/3265509999`.
ashley: taking over :phone:. will escalate if any regression.
incident-bot: thread archived for on-call handoff.
